definitions.name: Target-excluded saturated off-target instrumental-variable class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal T,\mathcal C}=\{P: P\text{ is a law on the declared finite variables satisfying assumptions }\mathrm{ass:randomization},\mathrm{ass:positive\mbox{-}arm\mbox{-}probability},\mathrm{ass:target\mbox{-}exclusion},\mathrm{ass:exposure\mbox{-}consistency},\mathrm{ass:target\mbox{-}outcome\mbox{-}consistency},\mathrm{ass:offtarget\mbox{-}outcome\mbox{-}consistency}\}\).

definitions.name: Armwise off-target refinement
definitions.construction: For each reduced atom \(r=((x_z(r))_z,y_{\mathcal T}(r))\) drawn with mass \(q_r\), refine independently over \(z\). If \(x_z(r)=t\in\mathcal T\), set \(X_z=t\), retain \(Y_t=y_t(r)\), and set the unused coordinates \(R_{c,z}\) to zero. If \(x_z(r)=\star\), draw \((C_z,V_z)\sim\eta_z\), set \(X_z=C_z\), set \(R_{C_z,z}=V_z\), and set the other unused \(R_{c,z}\) to zero. Mixing these full atoms defines \(\mathfrak R_p(q)\); when \(s_z(\star)=0\), use any fixed boundary allocation because the corresponding branch has zero mass. Observed outcomes are assigned only by the target rule \(Y=Y_t\) on \(\{X=t\}\) and the arm-specific rule \(Y=R_{c,z}\) on \(\{X=c,Z=z\}\).

u)=\sigma\}\), where \(
u\) ranges over nonnegative integer count arrays with the fixed arm totals \(n_z\).

Finite-fiber fixed-nuisance convexification of a full-data rule
Reduced whole-set confidence region
definitions.construction: With \(\rho_z(\alpha)=[\log(m/\alpha)+(d-1)\log(n_z+1)]/n_z\), set \(\mathcal K_\alpha(\widehat s)=\{s'\in\mathcal S:D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat s_z\|s'_z)\le\rho_z(\alpha)\ \forall z\}\) and \(\widehat\Theta_\alpha=\bigcup_{s'\in\mathcal K_\alpha(\widehat s)}\Theta(s')\).

definitions.name: Vanishing-penalty active-cone handle
definitions.construction: Quadratically regularize \(q\mapsto u^\top Bq\) over \(F(s)\), enumerate the active dual cone as the penalty vanishes, and invert the resulting local Gaussian max functional.

definitions.name: Two-arm enumeration witness
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal Z=\{1,2\}\), \(\mathcal T=\{a,b\}\), and \(\mathcal C=\{c\}\), define \(p^{\mathrm w}_1(a,0)=p^{\mathrm w}_1(c,1)=1/2\), \(p^{\mathrm w}_2(a,0)=p^{\mathrm w}_2(c,0)=1/2\), and set every other cell to zero.

definitions.name: Exact response-type and linear-program certificate
definitions.construction: Enumerate the \(36\) reduced columns \( (x_1,x_2,y_a,y_b)\in\{a,b,\star\}^2\times\{0,1\}^2\), the \(144\) saturated columns \( (x_1,x_2,y_a,y_b,r_{c,1},r_{c,2})\in\{a,b,c\}^2\times\{0,1\}^4\), and the \(72\) common-response columns \( (x_1,x_2,y_a,y_b,r_c)\in\{a,b,c\}^2\times\{0,1\}^3\). For each list form its zero-one observed-cell incidence matrix \(G\), impose \(G\omega=p^{\mathrm w}\), \(\omega\ge0\), and \(\mathbf 1^\top\omega=1\), and minimize and maximize \(\sum_f\omega_f(y_b(f)-y_a(f))\). In the saturated program the lower endpoint is attained by mass \(1/2\) on each of \((a,a,0,0,0,0)\) and \((c,c,1,0,1,0)\), while the upper endpoint is attained by mass \(1/2\) on each of \((a,a,0,1,0,0)\) and \((c,c,0,1,1,0)\). The valid inequalities \(\tau\le1\) and \(\tau\ge-E[Y_a]\ge-1/2\), where \(P(Y_a=0)\ge P(X_1=a\text{ or }X_2=a)\ge1/2\), certify those saturated optima. Under the common-response restriction the lower endpoint is attained by mass \(1/2\) on each of \((c,a,0,0,1)\) and \((a,c,0,0,0)\), and the upper endpoint by the same two exposure-response columns with \(y_b=1\). The observed constraints make \(\{X_1=c,r_c=1\}\) and \(\{X_2=c,r_c=0\}\) disjoint events of total probability one and force \(Y_a=0\), certifying \(0\le\tau\le1\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal T,\mathcal C}\) with \(\lambda_z=P(Z=z)>0\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\), observed conditional arm law \(p\), and skeleton \(s\), \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm F}(p)=\Theta(s)\). More precisely, \(A\kappa_{\#}\pi=s\) and \(B\kappa_{\#}\pi=B_{\mathrm F}\pi\) for every feasible full law \(\pi\); conversely, for every \(q\in F(s)\), the explicit refinement satisfies \(A_{\mathrm F}\mathfrak R_p(q)=p\), \(\kappa_{\#}\mathfrak R_p(q)=q\), and \(B_{\mathrm F}\mathfrak R_p(q)=Bq\), including every zero-\(\star\)-mass boundary. Hence the sharp set and the dimensions \(|\mathcal R|=(|\mathcal T|+1)^m2^{|\mathcal T|}\) and \(md\) are independent of \(|\mathcal C|\). This strictly extends Results 1 and 3 of Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander from their specified low-cardinality target contrasts to the complete law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\) for arbitrary finite \(m,\mathcal T,\mathcal C\).
statements.justification: This equality identifies exactly which observed information survives when only target exposure interventions are scientifically meaningful.
statements.gap: Gabriel et al. prove specified low-cardinality target-contrast cases; this theorem extends that axis to arbitrary finite \(m,\mathcal T,\mathcal C\), the complete law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\), and a boundary-safe right inverse. Song et al. are an adjacent arbitrary-cardinality benchmark under exclusion for every exposure level, not the theorem being extended.
statements.consumer: Dose, adherence, and Mendelian-randomization studies may retain many irregular realized exposure levels without enlarging the identification computation for a selected target contrast.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\), \(m=2\), and \(\mathcal T=\{a,b\}\), then \(\Theta(s)\) is the classical binary response-type polytope and the extrema of \(\tau=E[Y_b-Y_a]\) are the Balke--Pearl sharp bounds.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against the canonical binary instrumental-variable model.
statements.gap: This is a known special case and is included as a validation result rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementers can unit-test the reduced incidence matrix against published Balke--Pearl formulas.

statements.statement: For \(m\ge2\) and nonempty \(\mathcal C\), the common-response restriction \(R_{c,z}=R_c\) defines a strict submodel \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\subsetneq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\). For \(p^{\mathrm w}\) on arms \(\{1,2\}\), the response-type certificate \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm w}\) exhaustively enumerates \(|\mathcal R|=36\), \(|\mathcal R_{\mathrm F}|=144\) under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\), and \(72\) types under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\). Its feasible primal mixtures and valid endpoint inequalities certify \(\tau\in[-1/2,1]\) under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\) and \(\tau\in[0,1]\) under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\).
statements.justification: The strict inclusion and witness separate saturated arm-specific off-target responses from the common-response submodel relevant to the fully excluded benchmark.
statements.gap: Song et al. identify the larger all-exposure potential-outcome law under common excluded responses, whereas this proposition certifies that relaxing exclusion on \(\mathcal C\) can change bounds for a target-only contrast.
statements.consumer: The witness is an exact regression test for response-type software and for the right-inverse implementation.

statements.statement: Conditional on \((n_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\), the likelihood of \(N\) under every \((q,\eta)\) factors as \(\prod_{z\in\mathcal Z}L_z(N_z;(Aq)_z,\eta_z)\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:skeleton\mbox{-}factorization}\). The parameter space is the Cartesian product \(\{q:q\in\Delta^{|\mathcal R|-1}\}\times\mathcal E_{\mathcal C}^m\); conditional on \(S\), the off-target allocation counts depend on \(\eta\) but not on \(q\).
statements.justification: Factorization turns identification irrelevance into a precise statistical separation without falsely labeling the detailed counts ancillary.
statements.gap: Categorical instrumental-variable inference is written for the full multinomial law, and no located result isolates this variation-independent off-target allocation nuisance.
statements.consumer: Decision rules and confidence procedures can be designed on the skeleton experiment even when the data retain thousands of off-target labels.

statements.statement:
Conditional on fixed finite arm counts \((n_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\), for every full-data rule \(\delta\), fixed nuisance point \(\eta^0\), and reduced law \(q\), the fiber \(\Omega(\sigma)=\{
u:S(
u)=\sigma\}\) is finite for every \(\sigma\), and \(\delta_0(\sigma)=\sum_{
u\in\Omega(\sigma)}K_{\eta^0}(
u\mid\sigma)\delta(
u)\in\mathcal A\). This rule satisfies \(R_q(\delta_0)\le R_{q,\eta^0}(\delta)\le\sup_\eta R_{q,\eta}(\delta)\). Conversely, every skeleton rule \(\phi\) lifts to the full-data rule \(\delta^{\phi}(
u)=\phi(S(
u))\), for which \(R_{q,\eta}(\delta^{\phi})=R_q(\phi)\) for all \(q,\eta\). Therefore \(\inf_\delta\sup_{q,\eta}R_{q,\eta}(\delta)=\inf_\phi\sup_qR_q(\phi)\). No pointwise inequality \(R_{q,\eta}(\delta_0)\le R_{q,\eta}(\delta)\) is asserted for arbitrary \(\eta\).
statements.justification: Because fixed arm counts and finite alphabets make every \(\Omega(\sigma)\) finite, the barycenter exists for every rule and lies in the convex action space without closedness or integrability conditions; likelihood factorization makes \(K_{\eta^0}\) independent of \(q\), and Jensen's inequality gives the first risk bound.
statements.gap: Blackwell comparison does not directly apply because the conditional allocation kernel contains an unknown nuisance; the supremum over the variation-independent nuisance is the new step.
statements.consumer: A minimax analyst loses nothing by storing and processing only target cells and total off-target counts.

statements.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal T,\mathcal C}\), and every off-target allocation \(\eta\), \(P\{\Theta(s)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_\alpha\mid(n_z)_z\}\ge1-\alpha\). The event follows from \(P\{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat s_z\|s_z)>\rho_z(\alpha)\}\le\alpha/m\) and therefore remains valid at endpoint kinks and simultaneously for every linear functional of \(\operatorname{law}(Y_{\mathcal T})\). Calibration and every optimization dimension are independent of \(|\mathcal C|\); direct response-type computation uses \((|\mathcal T|+1)^m2^{|\mathcal T|}\) columns and is exponential only in \(m\) and \(|\mathcal T|\).
statements.justification: The guarantee protects the complete sharp set in finite samples without selecting an active endpoint formula.
statements.gap: Song et al. project a full-alphabet KL region under full exclusion; this theorem first quotients the weaker target-only model and removes \(|\mathcal C|\) from calibration and computation.
statements.consumer: Analysts with finely coded nonadherence or dosage deviations obtain honest whole-set uncertainty without merging scientific target levels.

statements.statement: The compatible-fiber modulus \(H_A\) is finite and admits a computable upper certificate obtained by enumerating the full-row-rank active submatrices of the equality-plus-nonnegativity system for \(F(s)\). For all \(s,s'\in\mathcal S\), \(e_1(\Theta(s'),\Theta(s))\le H_A\|s'-s\|_1\) and \(|h_{s'}(u)-h_s(u)|\le H_A\|u\|_\infty\|s'-s\|_1\). On the coverage event in Theorem 5, \(e_1(\widehat\Theta_\alpha,\Theta(s))\le2H_A\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\sqrt{2\rho_z(\alpha)}\). Every constant depends only on \(A\) and \(B\), hence on \(m\) and \(|\mathcal T|\), not on \(|\mathcal C|\).
statements.justification: This converts sampling error in the reduced multinomial law into deterministic excess width for every target-law direction.
statements.gap: Hoffman and Li provide generic polyhedral sensitivity, but no published instrumental-variable result gives this compatible-simplex support modulus or its quotient-invariant confidence-width consequence.
statements.consumer: The bound supplies stopping rules, sample-size calculations, and numerical tolerances for projected target-law regions.

statements.statement: Under the interior, feasible-direction, regular-face, nonzero-derivative, and arm-proportion conditions, there exist constants \(c>0\) and \(c_0>0\) such that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sqrt n\inf_{\widehat h}\sup_{e\in\{-c,c\}}E_{s_0+ev/\sqrt n,\eta}|\widehat h-h_{s_0+ev/\sqrt n}(u_0)|\ge c_0\), even when \(\widehat h\) uses the full counts \(N\). The constants and the lower bound are uniform over the labels and cardinality of \(\mathcal C\).
statements.justification: The local two-point bound certifies that root-\(n\) width on a regular face cannot be improved by retaining off-target labels.
statements.gap: Existing endpoint work gives upper inference results or generic regularization, not a target-quotient lower bound uniform in off-target refinement.
statements.consumer: The result benchmarks the order of projected-region width and prevents claims that a larger off-target alphabet can improve regular-face rates.

statements.statement: Using the vanishing-penalty active-cone handle, characterize the local asymptotic minimax risk and limit experiment for \(h_s(u)\) at every skeleton law where the reduced dual program has multiple optimal vertices, and construct one data-driven estimator and confidence procedure that attains the resulting face-by-face frontier without knowing the active cone.
statements.justification: The exact behavior at facet switches is the first-class open content left after finite-sample coverage and regular-face optimality.
statements.gap: Levis et al. use margins or smoothing and Gafarov uses generic quadratic regularization; neither supplies the exact target-IV local minimax phase diagram.
statements.consumer: An attaining procedure would replace conservative whole-set projection by shorter calibrated intervals whenever the observed skeleton is near, but not exactly on, a dual tie.

sampling_model.design: Randomized finite-arm instrument with \(\lambda_z=P(Z=z)>0\) for every population arm, with inference conditional on the realized positive arm counts \((n_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units from a law in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal T,\mathcal C}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The realized exposure lies in \(\mathcal X=\mathcal T\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal C\); target levels obey exclusion and off-target levels have saturated arm-specific responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Population positivity \(\lambda_z>0\) defines every conditional arm law \(p_z\) and skeleton law \(s_z\). The separate realized-sample condition \(n_z\ge1\) is required for finite-sample calibration; positive limiting arm proportions and an interior skeleton are used solely for the regular-face lower bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated: conditional on fixed finite arm counts, off-target allocations \(\eta_z\) factor variation-independently, induce finite-fiber kernels \(K_\eta(\nu\mid\sigma)\), and are removed before KL calibration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Results 1 and 3 give symbolically identical target-contrast bounds in specified two- and three-level instrument cases after adding one off-target level.
The binary instrumental-variable average treatment effect has sharp response-type linear-program bounds.

Theorem 1 characterizes the joint law of potential outcomes for all exposure levels under full exclusion at arbitrary finite cardinalities, and Theorem 4 gives simultaneous finite-sample intervals by KL projection.
Response-function variables convert a stated class of discrete causal queries into linear programs with tight symbolic bounds.
Theorem 1 gives an alphabet-generic polynomial bound for the moment-generating function of empirical multinomial relative entropy.
Randomization kernels and attainable risk sets characterize comparisons of statistical experiments.
A fixed consistent linear inequality system admits a uniform residual-to-solution distance constant.
Sharp right-hand-side Lipschitz constants for linear-program feasible and optimal solution sets can be expressed using constraint submatrices.
A margin condition yields root-\(n\) endpoint inference, while smooth approximations give conservative bounds for binary instrumental variables.
Quadratically regularized support values yield uniform Gaussian inference in polygonal affine identified models under stated regularity conditions.
Sharp analytical instrumental-variable bounds and testable implications require exponentially many linear pieces in the studied growing-support regimes.

tldr: Only selected levels of a finely recorded exposure may define meaningful interventions. Under positive-probability random assignment and exclusion restricted to those levels, the full categorical instrumental-variable model has an exact quotient: the sharp law of the target potential-outcome vector is the image of a reduced response simplex that keeps target outcome cells and one off-target mass per arm. An explicit boundary-safe right inverse proves independence from the number and labels of off-target categories. Conditional on fixed finite arm counts, the same quotient factors the experiment and yields equality of nuisance-minimax decision values for convex loss through a finite-fiber kernel. It also supports a finite-sample method-of-types confidence region for the entire sharp set whose calibration is independent of \(|\mathcal C|\). A compatible-fiber Hoffman theorem controls excess width, a local lower bound certifies the root-\(n\) regular-face rate, and the exact kink frontier remains the central open question.

project_justification.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander's target-level coarsening calculations stop at specified low cardinalities, whereas Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson's adjacent arbitrary-cardinality theory assumes excluded potential outcomes for every exposure category and identifies the larger all-exposure law. Full-alphabet inference consequently confounds scientific target dimension with arbitrary recording detail.
project_justification.niche: The relevant model has common potential outcomes only on \(\mathcal T\), saturated \(R_{c,z}\) on \(\mathcal C\), and asks for the whole law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\) rather than a single selected endpoint.
project_justification.fill: The quotient and its right inverse give sharp identification; the product likelihood and finite-fiber convexification give the exact nuisance-minimax comparison in the conditional finite-count experiment; reduced KL projection gives kink-robust finite-sample coverage; and polyhedral stability converts its radius to a target-set excess bound.

related_work: The field-tier comparison has two distinct axes. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander \cite{GabrielSachsSjolander2025} distinguish meaningful target levels from ill-defined or contaminated levels and prove specified low-cardinality target-contrast results; Theorem 1 strictly extends that line to arbitrary finite \(m,\mathcal T,\mathcal C\), the complete law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\), and a boundary-safe right inverse. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson \cite{SongGuoChanRichardson2024} are the adjacent arbitrary-cardinality fully excluded benchmark: their common-response restriction \(R_{c,z}=R_c\) is strictly contained in the saturated off-target class for \(m\ge2\) and nonempty \(\mathcal C\). Song et al. identify the larger all-exposure potential-outcome law under stronger exclusion, while Theorem 1 identifies the target marginal after exclusion is relaxed on \(\mathcal C\); Proposition 1 certifies that this relaxation changes target bounds. Their KL construction informs the reduced confidence region, but no equality between their projected set and \(\Theta(s)\) is claimed. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel \cite{SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2023} provide the response-function incidence machinery adapted by the quotient proof. Guo and Richardson \cite{GuoRichardson2021} provide the alphabet-generic relative-entropy concentration tool. Blackwell \cite{Blackwell1953} supplies the experiment-comparison template, while the unknown allocation kernel forces the nuisance-minimax rather than pointwise comparison. Hoffman \cite{Hoffman1952} and Li \cite{Li1993} supply generic polyhedral error-bound tools used to obtain the reduced causal modulus. Levis et al. \cite{LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025} and Gafarov \cite{Gafarov2025} locate the active-facet inference problem but do not solve the target-specific kink frontier. Boushehrian et al. \cite{BoushehrianBadriAkbariKiyavash2026} show why exponential dependence on substantive support can remain even after irrelevant off-target cardinality is removed.
technical_internal_limitation: The method-of-types radius is deliberately elementary and can be conservatively larger than the polynomial Chernoff calibration of Guo and Richardson. The novelty is the quotient that permits either calibration on \(d=2|\mathcal T|+1\) cells, not a new multinomial tail inequality. Song et al. remain an adjacent stronger-assumption benchmark for a larger all-exposure estimand; no equality with their projected set is asserted. The nuisance-minimax comparison is confined to the finite count experiment conditional on fixed arm counts; it does not assert a pointwise comparison at arbitrary \(\eta\) or an abstract infinite-sample-space theorem. The exact smallest Hoffman constant and the nonregular kink rate are not presupposed.
honest_scope: The equality of full and reduced identified images, the right inverse, the finite-count nuisance-minimax theorem, finite-sample whole-set coverage, the finite Hoffman certificate, and the regular-face lower bound are theorem obligations. The condition \(\lambda_z>0\) only makes the population conditional laws \(p_z\) and \(s_z\) well defined; it imposes no restriction on response types, feasible fibers, or the right-inverse equality. The separate condition \(n_z\ge1\) concerns the realized conditional sampling experiment. The minimax equality uses finite fibers and convexity only, so it requires neither closedness of \(\mathcal A\) nor an integrability assumption. The exact face-by-face minimax law and an adaptive attaining procedure at dual ties remain open. When \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\), \(m=2\), and \(|\mathcal T|=2\), the construction reduces to the classical Balke--Pearl response-type program.

seed_details.title: Target-specific exclusion quotient with a saturated off-target right inverse
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction and Results 1--3 on pp. 2--4 and 13--16, the response-function proof boundary on pp. 13--14, and the Discussion on pp. 22--23 of arXiv:2401.17735 were read.
seed_details.anchor_quote: Investigating if this pattern extends to higher levels of the exposure ... and if it can be proven for arbitrary levels.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The low-cardinality vertex-enumeration argument does not supply a surjection from arbitrary off-target refinements to a target-potential-outcome fiber. The first changed step is to collapse every off-target realized exposure to \(\star\), then explicitly lift each reduced atom by armwise conditional allocations \(\eta_z(c,y)\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for target-specific exclusion, off-target exposure quotients, arbitrary-cardinality coarsening, and categorical instrumental-variable response types located no theorem beyond the low-cardinality cases and the fully excluded categorical model.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. because their Theorem 1 already handles arbitrary finite categorical treatments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Song et al. define excluded potential outcomes for every treatment category and identify the larger all-exposure law under stronger assumptions. The target-only model deliberately has no common \(Y_c\) for \(c\in\mathcal C\), and equality with the reduced target image requires a new right inverse at positive and zero \(\star\)-mass.

seed_details.title: Nuisance-minimax equivalence of the full and skeleton experiments
seed_details.anchor_opened: The full-data categorical setup in Section 2, the identification construction in Theorem 1 and Supplement S2, the multinomial experiment in Section 6, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2405.09510v6 were read; Blackwell's publisher record was opened as the method thread.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The skeleton is not sufficient for \((q,\eta)\), so ordinary Rao--Blackwell pointwise domination is false. Conditional on fixed finite arm counts, the first changed step is to factor the multinomial likelihood, define \(K_{\eta^0}(\nu\mid\sigma)\) on the finite fiber \(\Omega(\sigma)\), and average a full-data rule by its finite barycenter before taking \(\sup_\eta\); the reverse direction lifts any skeleton rule by composition with \(S\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining categorical instrumental variables, skeleton counts, nuisance minimaxity, variation-independent allocations, and comparison of experiments found no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: The off-target labels are ancillary, so discarding them is an elementary sufficiency argument.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their conditional distribution depends on \(\eta\), making them non-ancillary for the full parameter and preventing a parameter-free pointwise Rao--Blackwell improvement; only the nuisance-supremum risk comparison survives.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample projection for the entire reduced identified set
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and Eq. 8, Section 6 and Theorem 4, the sufficiency construction in Supplement S2, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2405.09510v6 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Song et al. calibrate the full \(KM\)-cell arm law under exclusion for every treatment. The first changed step is to establish the target-only quotient before concentration, then project an armwise \(d=2|\mathcal T|+1\) method-of-types region to a union of complete reduced fibers.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for simultaneous finite-sample coverage of a target-potential-outcome identified set under partial exclusion and for calibration independent of off-target support found no direct result.
seed_details.red_team: This is only Song et al.'s confidence program after replacing its alphabet size.
seed_details.rebuttal: Replacing the alphabet is valid only after proving equality of the saturated full and reduced identified images; the resulting event covers the whole set at facet switches and is uniform over unrestricted off-target allocations.

seed_details.title: Global feasible-fiber and support-value modulus for the reduced incidence system
seed_details.anchor_opened: The main theorem, its active-halfspace proof on pp. 263--264, and the discussion of computable constants on pp. 264--265 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Hoffman's theorem controls distance to one fixed inequality system. The first changed step is a uniform restriction to compatible right-hand sides of the simplex equality fiber \(Aq=s\), followed by the stochastic target map \(B\) and support-function duality.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Hoffman constants, response-function instrumental-variable fibers, support-function perturbations, and off-target cardinality found generic polyhedral sensitivity results but no target-specific quotient modulus.
seed_details.red_team: The desired bound is a one-line corollary of the 1952 Hoffman lemma.
seed_details.rebuttal: The publishable content is the compatible-simplex fiber formulation, a finite active-system certificate, passage to all scalar support values, and its combination with the reduced KL region; generic theory alone does not state this \(|\mathcal C|\)-free causal modulus.

seed_details.title: Minimax phase diagram for regular faces and target-IV facet kinks
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorems 1--3, the margin construction in Sections 4--5, proof appendices, and the Discussion of arXiv:2301.12106v4 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Levis et al. obtain root-\(n\) inference under a margin condition or conservative smoothing for binary-IV formulas. The first changed step is to analyze the finite dual fan of the reduced arbitrary-cardinality LP and build local alternatives that cross a nonunique dual face.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches joining categorical-IV support endpoints, active-facet minimax rates, and off-target quotienting found regularized affine-model inference in Gafarov but no sharp target-IV kink phase diagram.
seed_details.red_team: Gafarov already gives uniform Gaussian inference for polygonal identified sets.
seed_details.rebuttal: Gafarov regularizes a generic affine model; it neither derives the exact local minimax law at target-IV dual ties nor proves invariance to arbitrary off-target refinements.

seed_details.title: Critical-violation frontier between a common off-target outcome and saturated arm responses
seed_details.anchor_opened: Results 1--3 and the Discussion of arXiv:2401.17735 were read, including the distinction between well-defined, ill-defined, and instrument-contaminated exposure levels.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace equality of off-target responses across arms by a total-variation budget \(\delta\), optimize target support values over the resulting coupling polytope, and derive the first \(\delta\) at which a sign conclusion changes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for critical-\(\delta\) sensitivity of off-target exclusion in categorical instrumental-variable bounds found qualitative contamination analyses but no derived frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The sensitivity curve is a routine parametric LP in \(\delta\).
seed_details.rebuttal: A useful result would require a sharp piecewise-linear envelope and a dual characterization of the critical \(\delta\), not merely resolving the LP on a grid.

seed_details.title: Covariate-conditional quotient and efficient regular-face endpoint estimation
seed_details.anchor_opened: The covariate-assisted Balke--Pearl setup, margin condition, influence-function expansion in Theorem 2, smooth approximation in Theorem 3, and Discussion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to prove the quotient pointwise in covariates and then differentiate an integrated reduced support value through its active dual basis.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for covariate-assisted categorical instrumental-variable bounds under target-only exclusion located binary fully excluded endpoint theory but no conditional quotient or efficiency bound.
seed_details.red_team: This is a mechanical conditional version of the finite quotient.
seed_details.rebuttal: The identification step is pointwise, but efficient estimation requires a new influence function for a covariate-indexed LP value and a margin condition on dual-basis switches.

seed_details.title: Closed nonredundant inequalities for the reduced target-law polytope
seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 1, the Strassen sufficiency argument in Supplement S2, and the nonredundancy analysis in Sections 4--5 of arXiv:2405.09510v6 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The proposed first step was to treat \(\star\) as an observed category with a deterministic response and eliminate its potential outcome from Song et al.'s inequalities.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search showed that this inequality family follows directly once the quotient theorem is known.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. by adding a deterministic \(\star\) category.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the inequality representation considered in isolation.

seed_details.title: Sharper Chernoff calibration on the reduced alphabet
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and its induction proof, the Chernoff inversion, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2003.08614 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The proposed first step was to substitute \(d=2|\mathcal T|+1\) into the polynomial moment-generating-function bound after quotienting.
seed_details.destination_search: The method paper already proves the required uniform multinomial inequality for every finite alphabet size.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Guo and Richardson because their theorem is alphabet-generic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; only the preceding quotient is new, so this cannot stand as a seed.

literature_map.settled: Binary- and ternary-instrument calculations show that selected target contrasts can retain familiar bounds when one off-target level is ill-defined or directly contaminated.
literature_map.open_boundary: The published Discussion explicitly leaves arbitrary exposure cardinality open, and the proof does not construct a cardinality-uniform right inverse.

literature_map.settled: Response-function and Strassen constructions characterize the larger joint all-exposure potential-outcome law when potential outcomes are defined and excluded for every treatment category.
literature_map.open_boundary: The relevant common-response restriction \(R_{c,z}=R_c\) is a strict submodel of the saturated off-target class for \(m\ge2\) and nonempty \(\mathcal C\); these papers do not identify the target marginal after that exclusion restriction is relaxed.

literature_map.settled: Uniform empirical-KL concentration and convex projection give simultaneous finite-sample intervals in the fully excluded categorical model.
literature_map.open_boundary: The published calibration uses the full observed alphabet; no located result first quotients unrestricted off-target allocations and covers the entire target-law set with dimension independent of \(|\mathcal C|\).

literature_map.settled: Randomization kernels characterize comparisons through attainable risk sets.
literature_map.open_boundary: The off-target allocation is parameter-dependent, so classical sufficiency does not yield pointwise domination; a nuisance-minimax reduction for this partially identified experiment is not covered.

literature_map.settled: Generic residual error bounds, right-hand-side LP sensitivity, margin-based endpoint inference, and regularized affine support inference are available.
literature_map.open_boundary: No source gives the reduced instrumental-variable simplex-fiber modulus, its \(|\mathcal C|\)-free KL consequence, or a sharp kink minimax phase diagram for this quotient.

literature_map.settled: Sharp analytical fully excluded instrumental-variable descriptions require exponentially many linear pieces in growing support regimes.
literature_map.open_boundary: The result does not remove an arbitrarily large unrestricted off-target alphabet before measuring complexity in \(m\) and \(|\mathcal T|\).
